title: Unified flywheel on real Emotion data
description:
## Purpose

Test the Unified Decision Flywheel (feature discovery from explanations, optimized fixed few-shot list, optional dynamic retrieval) on a REAL dataset where Jev starts weak, so the flywheel has something real to learn. The planted sports-vs-work corpus proved the machine works (A-c 0.83-0.87, A-c+F 0.85, D 0.89-0.92); real data was never tried. Replaces the Bias in Bios initiative (dropped: Jev already ~0.79, original loop +1.5 pts with a worse flip rate).

## Corpus

`dair-ai/emotion`, 6 classes (anger, fear, joy, love, sadness, surprise). Jev alone: zero-shot macro-F1 0.509 / acc 0.5915; best static retrieval (64/label) 0.649 / 0.694. Prepared: `studies/manifests/emotion.json`, HF cache `.data/huggingface/dair-ai___emotion`; Jev zero-shot answers for all 2,000 test items cached (`.data/dev/emotion.scoreboard2.sqlite`, jev-1.13.0), so the baseline is free.

## Approach

Parametrize `src/decision_flywheel_evaluations/unified_*.py` by a frozen `Corpus` config and `--corpus {planted,emotion}`; planted stays the default, byte-identical. 3 rounds x 150 labels from the pool; arms scored on dev-100 each round; nothing chosen on the final slice. Arms: 0 (free via cache), A-c, F, F-rand, A-c+F; optional D on the final slice only. Macro-F1 primary.

## Working rules (owner)

- Opus agents file plans in Kanbus (`kbs` only) before any build; builds are offline, small reviewed steps by Opus agents; the main session reviews, pushes and runs live stages.
- Small iterations (150 labels/round), development phase, no preregistration ceremony. Jev spend authorized within stated caps.
- Stop points where the owner looks before more is spent; ask the owner one plain question at a time, at the top of a message.
- Kanbus right_now summaries stay disabled in both repos.

## Cost cap

**Hard cumulative cap $10.** Upper bound ~13,000 Jev requests (~$1 per 1,000 few-shot requests; worst case ~$8); labeler (OpenAI gpt-6-luna) < $0.50. Real spend lower because of caching.

## Caveats (carry into the results)

- Emotion test items were exposed in earlier project work: exploratory, not confirmatory.
- Labels came from hashtags: no consistent hidden rubric; noise ceiling (~0.7 plausible).
- The labeler's reasons are rationalizations by a model that knows the answer.
- One seed. "surprise" is ~3.6% of test (dev-100 holds ~3-4): report per-class recall.

## What result changes what we build

- A-c+F does not beat ~0.649 macro-F1 (best static retrieval) on the final slice: report that the flywheel does not close the gap on noisy real labels; stop.
- D clearly wins: dynamic retrieval becomes the default for multi-class tasks.
- F does not beat F-rand again: drop the list optimizer in favour of a random fixed list.
- The feature cap fires every round: larger rounds or one combined few-shot feature.
- Cached answers cannot be reused (hash mismatch): arm 0 costs ~$0.60 more on the final slice.

## Definition of done

Final slice scored for the arms with macro-F1, accuracy, per-class recall, confusion matrix, top-label Brier/ECE and paired bootstrap next to the free baselines; addendum in `studies/UNIFIED_FLYWHEEL_RESULTS.md` with the caveats; each rule above answered.

Approved plan: `~/.claude/plans/i-put-you-in-sprightly-penguin.md` (owner-approved 2026-10-01).
